hints.title: Running Weight Ceiling Identification
hints.text: Calculate the running cumulative weight of passengers boarding by turn, finding the final passenger whose running total does not exceed 1000.

hints.title: Window Running Sum with Limit
hints.text: Compute sum of weight over turn in ascending order. Filter records where running weight <= 1000, sort descending by running weight, and limit to one.

hints.title: Last Person Query Blueprint
hints.text: with CumulativeQueue as (select person_name, sum(weight) over (order by turn asc) as total_weight from Queue) select person_name from CumulativeQueue where total_weight <= 1000 order by total_weight desc limit 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH CumulativeQueue AS (
    SELECT person_name,
           SUM(weight) OVER (ORDER BY turn ASC) AS total_weight
    FROM Queue
)
SELECT person_name
FROM CumulativeQueue
WHERE total_weight <= 1000
ORDER BY total_weight DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

variables: Q: number of passengers in queue
complexity.notes: Window running total ordered by turn and limit-one filtering runs in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Self-joins comparing cumulative turns create quadratic comparisons across long queues.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window running sum evaluates prefix totals in a single pass over sorted turns.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of SUM(weight) OVER(ORDER BY turn ASC) filtered by <= 1000 and LIMIT 1.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def last_passenger(queue: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    queue = queue.sort_values(by='turn')
    queue['total_weight'] = queue['weight'].cumsum()
    valid = queue[queue['total_weight'] <= 1000]
    last = valid.iloc[[-1]]
    return last[['person_name']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Cumsum Filter and Tail Selection
